findings.title: Create a fresh queue pool for each partition assignment
findings.body: The factory creates one queue pool in its constructor and reuses it for every strategy. However, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts that pool down. Arroyo closes and recreates strategies when partition assignments change, so after the first rebalance the replacement strategy receives queues whose workers have stopped (and whose queues have been shut down). New results can no longer be processed; submission errors are caught and marked complete, potentially committing results that were never handled. Allocate assignment-scoped pools and offset trackers rather than reusing the closed pool.

findings.title: Bound queued work and propagate backpressure
findings.body: queue.Queue() has no size limit, and submit() always accepts more work without signaling backpressure to Arroyo. If a worker blocks or incoming results exceed processing throughput, the consumer continues reading Kafka and retains every decoded result, original message, and tracked offset in memory. This can exhaust process memory rather than leaving the backlog in Kafka. Use bounded queues and reject submissions for retry when capacity is reached.

findings.title: Do not require Kafka offsets to be numerically contiguous
findings.body: The tracker stops at any integer offset absent from all_offsets, even if every delivered record before the next outstanding record has completed. Kafka can legitimately deliver nonconsecutive offsets, for example because of transactional records or compaction. If offsets 100, 102, and 103 are delivered and completed before a commit, this code commits only 100 and then remains stuck on the nonexistent 101 while 102 and 103 remain tracked. Track completion in delivered-record order rather than requiring every integer offset to exist.

findings.title: Drain accepted work before stopping workers on graceful close
findings.body: Setting worker.shutdown to True makes each worker exit its loop after its current item, leaving queued items unprocessed despite shutdown(immediate=False). Strategy.close() also stops the commit loop before shutting down the workers, so results completed during shutdown never receive a final commit, and join() merely repeats close() rather than draining work. On shutdown or rebalance this abandons accepted results and replays already processed results; a worker that exceeds the five-second join can also continue processing after ownership is relinquished. Graceful close/join should drain accepted work, wait within the supplied timeout, and commit completed offsets before stopping; reserve abandonment for terminate().
